title: Emmett Johnson is on pace to become an elite running back
text:
Emmett Johnson has been impressive through two seasons in Nebraska’s backfield. The junior running back’s journey has been intriguing during his time in Lincoln. To become an elite running back in today’s landscape of college football, the ability to run and catch is as important as ever.
Below will be a comparison of Johnson to three former Husker running backs [Ameer Abdullah, Rex Burkhead and Roy Helu] with their statistics through their first two seasons in Lincoln. The data was gathered from sports-reference.com. The file was edited to only compare the first two seasons for each running back.
Let’s start with the main statistic, rushing:


Code
Rush_Stats |> 
  gt() |>
  cols_label(
    RushYds = "Yards",
    RushAvg = "Average",
    RushTD = "TDs",
    Name = "Athlete",
    Class = "Year",
    Att = "Attempts"
  ) |>
  fmt_number(
    columns = c(RushYds, Att),
    decimals = 0,   
    use_seps = TRUE) |>
  tab_header(
    title = "Is Emmett Johnson on pace to be in the same realm of these former Husker RBs with his rushing numbers?",
    subtitle = "Through two seasons, the stats say yes" ) |>
  tab_source_note(source_note=md("By: Bobby Schneider | Source: sportsreference.com")) |>
      tab_style(
        style = cell_text(color = "black", weight ="bold", align = "left"),
        locations = cells_title("title") )  |>
          tab_style(
    style = cell_text(color = "red", align = "left"),
    locations = cells_title("subtitle"))

It’s clear that Johnson is on the right pace through to seasons. The 4.9 average yards-per-carry is right with Abdullah and Burkhead. Helu had a 5.9 average, but his amount of carries was significantly less than Abdullah, Burkhead and Johnson.
The total rushing yardage Johnson comes in third, just three yards above Helu, but once again, the amount of carries is less than Abdullah and Burkhead. There were numerous times over the last two seasons where Johnson would get minimal touches.
Moreover, Johnson’s rushing touchdowns were less than each of the three running backs he’s compared to, yet Nebraska’s offense as a whole was less productive during Johnson’s two seasons getting carries.
The receiving numbers set Johnson apart. Here are the receiving statistics for Johnson, Burkhead, Abdullah and Helu through two seasons:


Code
ggplot() + 
  geom_beeswarm(data=Rec_Stats, aes(x=Rec, y=RecYds), color="red") +
 geom_text_repel(
    data=Rec_Stats, 
    aes(x=Rec, y=RecYds, label=Name))+
theme_minimal() +
labs(
    x = "Receptions", y = "Receiving Yards",
    title = "Johnson's got it won when it comes to catching the ball out of the backfield",
    subtitle = "Imagine the numbers Johnson could put up with a whole year of Holgorsen's savvy scheme",
    caption = "By: Bobby Schneider | Source: sportsreference.com"
  ) +
 theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", color = "black"),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(color = "red")
  )









Johnson’s redshirt freshman season he only had 46 receiving yards, but looking at his sophomore campaign, he tore it apart. Johnson jumped his receiving yardage to 286 as a sophomore wearing the scarlet and cream.
The top two red dots (the one at the very top, shows the total through two seasons) in the upper right corner, makes the jump that Johnson made in his second season stand out. He had the best of the three in total receiving yards and receptions out of the backfield with 332 yards racked up through the air. Johnson’s ability to be a jack of all trades could help him continue to be just as, if not more productive for the next two seasons.
So, how does Johnson’s rushing and receiving put together compare?
Here are the all-purpose yards produced for each of the four running backs:


Code
ggplot() + 
  geom_bar(data=AP_Stats, aes(x= Name, weight=APYds, fill="All-Purpose Yardage")) + 
  coord_flip() +
  theme_minimal()+
labs(
    x = "Player", y = "All-Purpose Yards",
    title = "Capping it off with the all-purpose yardage",
    subtitle = "He's a little behind Burkhead and Abdullah, yet he's on trending towards them",
    caption = "By: Bobby Schneider | Source: sportsreference.com"
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::comma) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(color = "red")
  )









Johnson’s behind Abdullah and Burkhead through two years in terms of all-purpose yardage, but is above Helu. Johnson is on the right road. He is within spitting distance in some categories, and some ahead.
The main purpose wasn’t to say Johnson is a better back, it was to prove that he has the potential to have a similar amount of production that these three backs had during their Husker football careers.
The rushing yardage might not reach the other three, but the all-purpose output very well could with Johnson’s ability to catch the ball out of the backfield, especially with offensive coordinator Dana Holgorsen in command.
Overall, the junior Husker running back should be set to have quite the breakthrough junior season in Nebraska’s backfield. It will be intriguing to compare Johnson to these three after his junior season.

title: Dylan Raiola compared to four returning Big Ten QBs
text:
Dylan Raiola showed sparks of eliteness as a true freshman in Lincoln, but he also had his fair share of rookie moments. As he enters his sophomore season, the expectations for Nebraska football with him under center continue to grow.
Could Raiola make the jump to become elite as a Big Ten QB? You’ll find he did pretty solid, especially compared to quarterbacks that had been starters before Raiola even stepped foot on a college campus.
Below, we will compare Raiola to four quarterbacks who were starters the past season in the Big Ten. The only expectation — former Tennessee, now UCLA quarterback Nico Iamaleava. The others include Penn State’s Drew Allar, Illinois’ Luke Altmyer and USC’s Jayden Maiava.


Code
waffle(
        Pass_Yards, 
        rows = 10, 
        title="Passing Yards", 
        xlab="1 square = 150 yards", 
        colors = c("#E41C38", "#2D68C4", "#E84A27", "#041E42", "#FFC72C")
)+
labs(
    title="Looking at passing yards, where's Raiola?", 
    subtitle = "Raiola comes in ranked second",
caption = "By: Bobby Schneider | Source: sportsreference.com")











Code
Raiola_B1G_QBs |>
  ggplot() + 
  geom_point(aes(x = Completion_Percentage, y = Attempts), color = "black") +
  geom_text_repel(
    aes(x = Completion_Percentage, y = Attempts, label = Name, color = Name)
  ) + 
  scale_color_manual(
    values = c(
      "Dylan Raiola" = "#E41C38",
      "Nico Iamaleava" = "#2D68C4",
      "Luke Altmyer" = "#E84A27",
      "Drew Allar" = "#041E42",
      "Jayden Maiava" = "#FFC72C"
    )
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::label_number(suffix = "%")) +
  theme_minimal()+
  labs( x = "Completion Percentage", y = "Attempts",
    title="Let's look at who has the best completion percentage", 
    subtitle = "Look at that, Raiola has the most attempts and still the highest percentage",
    caption = "By: Bobby Schneider | Source: sportsreference.com"
  )











Code
ggplot() + 
  geom_dumbbell(
    data=TD_INT, 
    aes(y=Name, x=Touchdowns, xend=Interceptions),
    size = 2,
    colour = "grey",
    colour_x = "black",
    colour_xend = "red")+
  theme_minimal()+
  labs( x = "TD - INT Rate", y = "Player",
    title="Touchdown to interception rate", 
    subtitle = "This is where Raiola lacks - TDs are black and INTs are red",
    caption = "By: Bobby Schneider | Source: sportsreference.com"
  ) 











Code
ggplot() +
  geom_beeswarm(
    data = Raiola_B1G_QBs, 
    aes(x = Y.G, y = QBR), color = "black"
  ) + 
  geom_text_repel(
    data = Raiola_B1G_QBs, 
    aes(x = Y.G, y = QBR, label = Name, color = Name), 
    show.legend = FALSE
  ) + 
  scale_color_manual(
    values = c(
      "Dylan Raiola" = "#E41C38",
      "Nico Iamaleava" = "#2D68C4",
      "Luke Altmyer" = "#E84A27",
      "Drew Allar" = "#041E42",
      "Jayden Maiava" = "#FFC72C"
    )
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Passing Yards Per Game", 
    y = "QBR",
    title = "Passing yards per game, along with QBR", 
    subtitle = "It's clear that the interceptions hurt Raiola's rating",
    caption = "By: Bobby Schneider | Source: sportsreference.com"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
